site.anchor: o dia que fixa a lei aplicável (art. 4º; Súmula 711 STF)

source.quote: Art. 4º - Considera-se praticado o crime no momento da ação ou omissão, ainda que outro seja o momento do resultado.

readings.description: The law in force when the continuation or permanence ceases governs the whole, even if more severe, provided it came into force before the cessation.
Art. 2º's lex mitior and art. 4º's 'momento da ação' fix the law at the first act, so a later, more severe law does not reach the conduct.
readings.rejection_rationale: STF Súmula 711 holds the more severe law applicable where its vigência precedes the cessation of the continuity or permanence.

taken.rationale: Settled by the STF's súmula. The `Fato no tempo` record carries `data da cessação da permanência ou da continuidade`; where it is present, `o dia que fixa a lei aplicável (art. 4º; Súmula 711 STF)` returns it, and `a lei do tempo do crime (art. 4º)` is the law in force that day.

settled_by.citation: Súmula 711: "A LEI PENAL MAIS GRAVE APLICA-SE AO CRIME CONTINUADO OU AO CRIME PERMANENTE, SE A SUA VIGÊNCIA É ANTERIOR À CESSAÇÃO DA CONTINUIDADE OU DA PERMANÊNCIA."

witnesses: cp-g1a-aplicacao-testes.l4: `o crime permanente que atravessou a lei nova` (begun 1.12.2014, ceased 1.2.2015) is governed by `a lei mais severa de 2015`; the same succession for an instantaneous crime on 1.12.2014 by the law of 2000
notes: Reserved id: sweep-a's M-sweep-a-16 opened this fork (sweep-a.forks-proposed.json). It spans arts. 2, 4 and 71; g1a owns the lowest-numbered article and creates it here. g1b, which encodes art. 71, cross-refers to it.
The same day governs art. 1º's question (was there a law defining the fact?) for a permanent crime that began before the incriminating law and went on after it.

delegated_field: Execução do crime's `a preparação do flagrante pela polícia tornou impossível a consumação` (and `havia vigilância ou segurança no local`, deliberately not read), in cp-g1a-crime.l4

site.anchor: crime impossível (art. 17)

source.quote: Art. 17 - Não se pune a tentativa quando, por ineficácia absoluta do meio ou por absoluta impropriedade do objeto, é impossível consumar-se o crime.

readings.description: A flagrante prepared by the police so that consummation is impossible is no crime; mere surveillance (electronic monitoring, security staff) does not by itself make the crime impossible.
Art. 17 reaches only absolute inefficacy of the means or absolute impropriety of the object; police preparation is outside it.
readings.rejection_rationale: STF Súmula 145 holds that there is no crime where the police's preparation of the flagrante makes consummation impossible.

readings.description: Any surveillance that would inevitably stop the theft makes it impossible within art. 17.
readings.rejection_rationale: STJ Súmula 567: surveillance or security staff inside a shop does not, by itself, make theft impossible.

taken.rationale: Settled by the two súmulas. Whether the preparation made consummation impossible is a finding on the facts; `crime impossível (art. 17)` reads it as a third limb beside the means and the object, and does not read the surveillance field at all, so surveillance alone never sets it.

settled_by.citation: Súmula 145: "NÃO HÁ CRIME, QUANDO A PREPARAÇÃO DO FLAGRANTE PELA POLÍCIA TORNA IMPOSSÍVEL A SUA CONSUMAÇÃO." (read with STJ Súmula 567 on surveillance, M-sweep-a-19)

witnesses: cp-g1a-crime-testes.l4: `o flagrante preparado` is a crime impossível; `o furto no mercado vigiado` is not, and its attempt is punishable
notes: Reserved id: sweep-a's M-sweep-a-18 opened it, with M-sweep-a-19; sweep-b's M-sweep-b-33 (Súmula 567 at art. 155) is subsumed by it.

site.anchor: as leis posteriores ao crime (art. 2º)
provisions: CP art. 2º, caput e parágrafo único

source.quote: A lei posterior, que de qualquer modo favorecer o agente, aplica-se aos fatos anteriores, ainda que decididos por sentença condenatória transitada em julgado.

readings.description: Any law that came into force after the crime counts as 'lei posterior', including one that was itself revoked before the decision (the lei intermediária): a milder one reaches the fact, and one that stopped treating it as a crime abolished it for good.
Only the law in force when the case is decided is compared with the law of the time; an intermediate law no longer in force has no effect.
readings.rejection_rationale: The text asks only that the law be later than the fact ('fatos anteriores'), not that it still be in force; the parágrafo único reaches facts already decided by a final judgment, so the comparison is not tied to the moment of decision.

taken.rationale: `as leis posteriores ao crime (art. 2º)` takes every law whose vigência began after the day that fixes the law and no later than the day of the decision, whatever its end.

witnesses: cp-g1a-aplicacao-testes.l4: `a lei intermediária mais branda` (2012–2014) reaches a fact of 2010 decided in 2020; `a lei intermediária abolicionista` abolished it

site.anchor: as leis posteriores mais favoráveis (art. 2º, parágrafo único)

source.quote: A lei posterior, que de qualquer modo favorecer o agente, aplica-se aos fatos anteriores

readings.description: The judge compares whole laws and applies the more favourable one entire; favourable parts of the later law may not be combined with favourable parts of the earlier one.

citations.cite: STJ, Súmula 501 (Terceira Seção, j. 23.10.2013, DJe 28.10.2013): "... desde que o resultado da incidência das suas disposições, na íntegra, seja mais favorável ao réu ..., sendo vedada a combinação de leis."

readings.description: 'De qualquer modo favorecer' lets the judge take the favourable provisions of each law and combine them.
readings.rejection_rationale: STJ Súmula 501: combining laws is forbidden, since it would create a third norm neither legislature enacted.

citations.cite: CP art. 2º, parágrafo único — "de qualquer modo"

taken.rationale: The encoding compares laws only through the judge's finding on each whole law (`favorece o agente em relação à lei do tempo do crime, segundo o juiz`) and returns whole laws, never parts. Where several later laws favour the agent it lists them all; which is the most favourable is the judge's comparison.

settled_by.authority: Superior Tribunal de Justiça, Terceira Seção
settled_by.citation: Súmula 501: "É cabível a aplicação retroativa da Lei n. 11.343/2006, desde que o resultado da incidência das suas disposições, na íntegra, seja mais favorável ao réu do que o advindo da aplicação da Lei n. 6.368/1976, sendo vedada a combinação de leis."

notes: The súmula's text is about the drug law of 2006, and states the general rule in its last clause. It was read in a secondary compilation (Trilhante) on 2026-09-29; the STJ's own archive page answered HTTP 403. The sweep (sweep-a) did not list it; the conductor may want sweep-a to record it as an interpretive entry.
Divergence 'none': the encoding has no way to express a combination, so the demoted reading cannot be exhibited.

site.anchor: a lei excepcional ou temporária rege o fato praticado durante sua vigência (art. 3º)

source.quote: Art. 3º - A lei excepcional ou temporária, embora decorrido o período de sua duração ou cessadas as circunstâncias que a determinaram, aplica-se ao fato praticado durante sua vigência.

readings.description: The exceptional or temporary law governs the facts of its period after it lapses; its lapse is no abolitio (art. 2º, caput), and the ordinary regime after it is no 'lei posterior mais favorável' (art. 2º, parágrafo único).

citations.cite: CP art. 3º — "embora decorrido o período de sua duração ... aplica-se ao fato praticado durante sua vigência"

readings.description: The Constitution's 'a lei penal não retroagirá, salvo para beneficiar o réu' (CF art. 5º, XL) admits no exception, so a milder later law reaches even the facts of a temporary law.
readings.foreclosure: The Code's own text says the opposite and no ruling of the STF or STJ displacing art. 3º was found by the sweep; the encoding follows the text.

taken.rationale: Art. 3º is written to override art. 2º for exactly this case; without it a temporary law would be unenforceable after it lapsed. `abolitio criminis (art. 2º, caput)` and `as leis posteriores mais favoráveis (art. 2º, parágrafo único)` both except the fact whose law of the time was exceptional or temporary.

witnesses: cp-g1a-aplicacao-testes.l4: `o fato durante a lei temporária` (June 2020) is governed by `a lei temporária de 2020` in 2022, though `o regime comum de 2021` no longer makes it a crime

site.anchor: a bordo, aplica-se a lei brasileira (art. 5º)

source.quote: bem como as aeronaves e as embarcações brasileiras, mercantes ou de propriedade privada, que se achem, respectivamente, no espaço aéreo correspondente ou em alto-mar.

citations.cite: CP art. 5º, § 2º — "em vôo no espaço aéreo correspondente"

readings.description: In § 1º, 'respectivamente' pairs the aircraft with 'o espaço aéreo correspondente' and the vessels with 'alto-mar', so the airspace is the one over the high seas. In § 2º, the same words mean the airspace over the national territory.
'Espaço aéreo correspondente' in § 1º is the airspace over the national territory, as in § 2º.
readings.rejection_rationale: A Brazilian aircraft in Brazil's airspace is already in the national territory (caput); the extension in § 1º would add nothing, and the high-seas airspace, which only § 1º could reach, would be left out.

taken.rationale: `Onde se encontrava` has distinct members for the airspace over the high seas and over Brazil, and the rule pairs each with the craft the text names.

witnesses: cp-g1a-aplicacao-testes.l4: a Brazilian private aircraft `no espaço aéreo correspondente ao alto-mar` is under Brazilian law; one `em território estrangeiro` is not

site.anchor: o efeito da pena cumprida no estrangeiro (art. 8º)

source.quote: Art. 8º - A pena cumprida no estrangeiro atenua a pena imposta no Brasil pelo mesmo crime, quando diversas, ou nela é computada, quando idênticas.

readings.description: 'Idênticas' means of the same kind among art. 32's three (custodial, restrictive of rights, fine): a custodial sentence served abroad is deducted from a custodial one imposed here.
'Idênticas' requires the same species of custodial penalty (reclusão against reclusão); a detenção served abroad only attenuates a reclusão imposed here.
readings.rejection_rationale: Foreign law does not use art. 33's species, so the comparison could rarely be made; a deduction of time served is what 'computada' asks for, and time is time.

readings.description: 'Idênticas' means the same penalty in kind and quantity.
readings.rejection_rationale: If the quantities had to be equal, 'computada' would always leave nothing to serve, and the paragraph would not need two words.

taken.rationale: `Pena cumprida no estrangeiro` records each side's `Espécie de pena` (cp-pena's art. 32 enum), and the rule compares them.

witnesses: cp-g1a-aplicacao-testes.l4: two years of custody served abroad against five imposed here leave three; custody against a restrictive penalty attenuates, and the rule refuses to compute by how much

site.anchor: a situação de legítima defesa (art. 25)
provisions: CP art. 25, caput e parágrafo único

source.quote: Art. 25 - Entende-se em legítima defesa quem, usando moderadamente dos meios necessários, repele injusta agressão, atual ou iminente, a direito seu ou de outrem.

citations.cite: STF, ADPF 779, Plenário, acórdão de 1.8.2023, DOU 10.8.2023

readings.description: The reading-down binds the courts from the STF's decision, whatever the date of the fact: every decision on or after 1.8.2023 excludes the honour thesis. Before that date, how the thesis stood under the text alone is not encoded.

citations.cite: STF, ADPF 779 — interpretação conforme, erga omnes and binding (Lei 9.882/1999)

readings.description: The reading-down is treated like a harsher law: it reaches only facts on or after 1.8.2023.
readings.foreclosure: An interpretação conforme declares what the text, read with the Constitution, always meant; it is not a later law, and art. 2º's rules about later laws do not govern it. No ruling limiting ADPF 779 to later facts was found.

taken.rationale: Every rule that reads art. 25 takes `a data da decisão`; `a situação de legítima defesa (art. 25)` is FALSE for the honour thesis from 1.8.2023 and refuses by name before it. The L4 rule-version axis (`RULES EFFECTIVE DATE`) would express the same thing, but unpinned it needs a document TIMEZONE and reads the wall clock (probe, notes/g1a.md), so an explicit parameter was used.

witnesses: cp-g1a-ilicitude-testes.l4: `a honra invocada` is no situation of legítima defesa on 1.8.2023 and in 2024; on 31.7.2023 the rule refuses
notes: The arm date is the merits acórdão's, as sweep entry M-sweep-a-01 gives it. The sweep did not check whether a medida cautelar bound the courts earlier; if one did, only `a data da ADPF 779` changes.

delegated_field: `Por que a execução iniciada não se consumou`'s members `o agente desistiu voluntariamente de prosseguir na execução` and `o agente impediu voluntariamente que o resultado se produzisse`, in cp-g1a-crime.l4

site.anchor: desistência voluntária (art. 15)

source.quote: Art. 15 - O agente que, voluntariamente, desiste de prosseguir na execução ou impede que o resultado se produza, só responde pelos atos já praticados.

citations.cite: CP art. 65, III, b — "por sua espontânea vontade"

readings.description: The desistance or prevention need be voluntary, the agent's own choice, even if someone else suggested it; it need not be spontaneous.

citations.cite: CP art. 65, III, b — "espontânea vontade", a different word where the Code wants spontaneity

readings.description: Only a desistance that arises from the agent alone, unprompted, benefits from art. 15.
readings.rejection_rationale: The Code says 'voluntariamente' here and 'espontânea vontade' in art. 65, III, b; it chose different words for different requirements.

taken.rationale: The finding is named with the Code's word 'voluntariamente'; the fact-finder certifies it. A desistance forced by an outside obstacle is not voluntary: that case is `por circunstâncias alheias à vontade do agente`, an attempt.

site.anchor: incide a diminuição do art. 16

source.quote: até o recebimento da denúncia ou da queixa, por ato voluntário do agente, a pena será reduzida de um a dois terços. (Redação dada pela Lei nº 7.209, de 11.7.1984)

readings.description: 'Até o recebimento' includes the day the charge is received.
The reparation must come before the receipt, so a reparation on the day of receipt is late.
readings.rejection_rationale: 'Até' marks a limit reached, not one excluded; the Code says 'antes' where it means before (e.g. art. 65, III, b, 'antes do julgamento').

citations.cite: CP art. 65, III, b — "antes do julgamento"

taken.rationale: The rule compares the reparation's day AT MOST the receipt's day.

witnesses: cp-g1a-crime-testes.l4: reparation on 1.8.2026 with the charge received on 1.8.2026 is in time; on 2.8.2026 it is not

delegated_field: `Reparação do dano`'s `data da reparação do dano ou da restituição da coisa`, in cp-g1a-crime.l4

site.anchor: Reparação do dano

source.quote: reparado o dano ou restituída a coisa, até o recebimento da denúncia ou da queixa, por ato voluntário do agente, a pena será reduzida de um a dois terços. (Redação dada pela Lei nº 7.209, de 11.7.1984)

readings.description: 'Reparado o dano ou restituída a coisa' means the whole damage repaired, or the whole thing returned; a partial reparation does not open art. 16.
A partial reparation opens art. 16, the fraction of reduction following how much was repaired.
readings.foreclosure: The text states a completed fact ('reparado o dano'), not a degree; the range of one to two thirds is the judge's to place, but not a license for a partial reparation. Whether the courts admit the partial case was not searched.

taken.rationale: The field records the day the damage was FULLY repaired or the thing returned; its herald says so, and a partial reparation is recorded as none.

site.anchor: legítima defesa do agente de segurança pública (art. 25, parágrafo único)

source.quote: Parágrafo único. Observados os requisitos previstos no caput deste artigo, considera-se também em legítima defesa o agente de segurança pública que repele agressão ou risco de agressão a vítima mantida refém durante a prática de crimes.

citations.cite: CP art. 25, parágrafo único (incluído pela Lei nº 13.964/2019)

readings.description: The paragraph adds no case: it demands every requisite of the caput, so a security officer who repels an aggression against a hostage is in legítima defesa exactly when the caput already says so.

citations.cite: CP art. 25, parágrafo único — "Observados os requisitos previstos no caput deste artigo"

readings.description: 'Agressão ou risco de agressão' reaches a risk short of an imminent aggression, widening legítima defesa for security officers.
readings.foreclosure: The paragraph's opening words require the caput's requisites, among them an aggression 'atual ou iminente'; a risk that is not imminent does not meet them.

citations.cite: CP art. 25, parágrafo único — "agressão ou risco de agressão"

taken.rationale: The rule requires `legítima defesa (art. 25, caput)` as its first limb, so it can never hold without the caput. For the same reason it needs no vigência gate: it cannot make a pre-2020 fact worse, and it makes none better.

notes: Shown declaratory, not divergent: cp-g1a-ilicitude-testes.l4: the hostage case holds under the paragraph and under the caput; immoderate, it holds under neither

delegated_field: `Situação de necessidade`'s `o agente provocou o perigo por sua vontade`, in cp-g1a-ilicitude.l4

site.anchor: há situação de necessidade (art. 24)

source.quote: que não provocou por sua vontade, nem podia de outro modo evitar, direito próprio ou alheio, cujo sacrifício, nas circunstâncias, não era razoável exigir-se. (Redação dada pela Lei nº 7.209, de 11.7.1984)

readings.description: 'Por sua vontade' bars only a danger the agent caused intentionally; one caused by negligence still allows estado de necessidade.
Any danger the agent caused, intentionally or by negligence, bars estado de necessidade.

taken.rationale: The field is named in the Code's words; the fact-finder decides whether a negligent provocation was 'por sua vontade'. The first reading is the one the words most directly carry, and the one the herald's wording suggests.

site.anchor: o efeito das excludentes de ilicitude (art. 23)

source.quote: Parágrafo único - O agente, em qualquer das hipóteses deste artigo, responderá pelo excesso doloso ou culposo.

readings.description: The agent answers only for an excess that was doloso or culposo; an excess with neither (an understandable overreaction the fact-finder attributes to neither intent nor negligence) is not punished.

citations.cite: CP art. 23, parágrafo único — "responderá pelo excesso doloso ou culposo"

readings.description: Once the limits are exceeded the justification fails entirely, and the agent answers for the crime as committed, whatever the modality of the excess.
readings.rejection_rationale: The paragraph confines liability to the doloso or culposo excess, and art. 18's parágrafo único punishes nothing without dolo or, where provided, culpa.

taken.rationale: `Modalidade do excesso` has only the doloso and culposo members; an excess with no modality found returns the named outcome `excesso sem dolo nem culpa, que o parágrafo único não pune (art. 23)`.

witnesses: cp-g1a-ilicitude-testes.l4: an immoderate defence with no modality found

site.anchor: as causas de diminuição cabíveis (arts. 26 e 28)

source.quote: A pena pode ser reduzida de um a dois terços, se o agente, em virtude de perturbação de saúde mental ou por desenvolvimento mental incompleto ou retardado não era inteiramente capaz de entender o caráter ilícito do fato ou de determinar-se de acordo com esse entendimento. (Redação dada pela Lei nº 7.209, de 11.7.1984)

readings.description: Once the requirements are met the reduction must be applied; the judge chooses only the fraction within the range.

citations.cite: CP art. 68 — the causes of decrease are applied in the third phase

readings.description: 'Pode'/'poderá': the judge may decline the reduction even when the requirements are met.

citations.cite: CP arts. 21, 24, § 2º, 26, parágrafo único, 28, § 2º, 29, § 1º — "pode", "poderá", against art. 16's "será"

taken.rationale: Recorded, not built in: the rules list each reduction as `cabível` (available) where its requirements are met and say nothing about whether the judge must apply it; the outcome names keep the Code's 'pode'. No authority was searched for any of the five articles; the question is left for a Brazilian criminal lawyer (notes/g1a.md).

notes: The same question g0 recorded for art. 155, § 2º (F-g0-27). The Code's own contrast is art. 16, 'será reduzida', encoded as mandatory.

site.anchor: o efeito do erro (art. 20)

source.quote: Não há isenção de pena quando o erro deriva de culpa e o fato é punível como crime culposo.

citations.cite: CP art. 20, caput — "exclui o dolo, mas permite a punição por crime culposo, se previsto em lei"

readings.description: A putative justification from an avoidable error is treated as an error on the tipo, like the caput whose paragraph it is: dolo is excluded, the culposo crime is punished where the law provides it, and where it does not, nothing is left to punish.

citations.cite: CP art. 20, caput and § 1º — the paragraph's second sentence names the consequence as punishment 'como crime culposo'

readings.description: An avoidable error on a justifying situation is an error on illicitude: the doloso crime stands, with art. 21's reduction.
readings.foreclosure: The paragraph's own sentence gives the culpable putative justification the culposo crime's punishment, which only the first reading explains; the second would punish it as doloso.

taken.rationale: `o efeito do erro (art. 20)` returns the named outcome `o erro deriva de culpa e o fato não é punível como crime culposo: não é punível (art. 20, § 1º, com o caput)`.

witnesses: cp-g1a-erro-testes.l4: a culpable putative defence where the crime has no culposo form

delegated_field: `Coação ou ordem`'s `o fato foi cometido em estrita obediência a ordem de superior hierárquico`, in cp-g1a-erro.l4

site.anchor: só é punível o autor da coação ou da ordem (art. 22)

source.quote: em estrita obediência a ordem, não manifestamente ilegal, de superior hierárquico

citations.cite: CP art. 65, III, c — "em cumprimento de ordem de autoridade superior"

readings.description: 'Superior hierárquico' is a superior in the public administration's hierarchy; an employer, a parent or a religious superior is not one.
Any relation of subordination, private employment included, gives a 'superior hierárquico'.
readings.rejection_rationale: An order the subordinate must obey without questioning its legality exists only in public hierarchy; the parallel attenuation of art. 65, III, c speaks of 'autoridade superior'.

taken.rationale: The finding is named in the Code's words; the fact-finder certifies that the superior was a hierarchical one. 'Coação irresistível' is read as moral coercion; physical force leaves no act of the coerced at all, and the rule answers the same (only the coercer punishable), so that second question has no divergence and is not a fork of its own.

site.anchor: cabe a diminuição do art. 26, parágrafo único
provisions: CP art. 26, caput e parágrafo único

source.quote: em virtude de perturbação de saúde mental ou por desenvolvimento mental incompleto ou retardado

citations.cite: CP art. 26, caput — "por doença mental ou desenvolvimento mental incompleto ou retardado"

readings.description: The caput exempts only for mental illness or incomplete or retarded development with total incapacity. Every other impairment — a mental illness that left some capacity (a 'perturbação de saúde mental' in the wider sense), or a disturbance that is not an illness even if it took all capacity — is the parágrafo único's reduction.

citations.cite: CP art. 26, caput and parágrafo único, as worded

readings.description: The degree decides: total incapacity from any mental cause exempts under the caput; partial incapacity from any cause, mental illness included, is the parágrafo único's.

taken.rationale: The caput names two causes and the parágrafo único names 'perturbação de saúde mental', a wider term; the encoding keeps the caput to its two causes and reads the parágrafo único's term to include a mental illness of lesser effect. The readings agree except on a non-illness disturbance that took all capacity, which the taken reading leaves to the parágrafo único. A mental-health expert's classification of such a case as 'doença mental' would move it to the caput under either reading.

witnesses: cp-g1a-imputabilidade-testes.l4: `perturbação de saúde mental` with no capacity left gives the parágrafo único's reduction, not the caput's exemption

site.anchor: o crime chegou, pelo menos, a ser tentado (art. 31)

source.quote: se o crime não chega, pelo menos, a ser tentado. (Redação dada pela Lei nº 7.209, de 11.7.1984)

citations.cite: CP art. 14, II — "tentado, quando, iniciada a execução, não se consuma por circunstâncias alheias à vontade do agente"

readings.description: 'Tentado' is art. 14, II's defined word: a crime the executor gave up by his own will (art. 15) did not reach an attempt, so the agreement, incitement or help behind it is not punishable either.
The crime 'reached an attempt' once execution began; the executor's desistance is personal to him (art. 30) and does not help the participant.
readings.foreclosure: The Code defines 'tentado' in art. 14, II and uses the same word here; a crime abandoned by the agent's will is outside that definition.

taken.rationale: `o crime chegou, pelo menos, a ser tentado (art. 31)` is consummation or cp-pena's `crime tentado (art. 14, II)`. An impossible crime (art. 17) did reach an attempt in that sense; it is art. 17 that leaves it unpunished.

witnesses: cp-g1a-concurso-testes.l4: the lookout's help where the executor desisted is not punishable; the instigation of an impossible crime is not excused by art. 31

delegated_field: `Concorrente`'s `participação de menor importância, segundo o juiz`, in cp-g1a-concurso.l4

site.anchor: cabe a diminuição do art. 29, § 1º

source.quote: § 1º - Se a participação for de menor importância, a pena pode ser diminuída de um sexto a um terço.

readings.description: 'Participação' is the participant's part (instigation, help), not the co-author's; a co-author cannot have a part of minor importance.
Any concorrente, co-authors included, may have had a part of minor importance.

citations.cite: CP art. 29, caput — "Quem, de qualquer modo, concorre"

taken.rationale: The finding is the judge's; the encoding does not compute it from the modes of concurring. Which reading the courts take was not searched; the question is listed for a Brazilian criminal lawyer.

site.anchor: a primeira pena é menos grave que a segunda

source.quote: Se algum dos concorrentes quis participar de crime menos grave, ser-lhe-á aplicada a pena deste; essa pena será aumentada até metade, na hipótese de ter sido previsível o resultado mais grave. (Redação dada pela Lei nº 7.209, de 11.7.1984)

readings.description: 'Menos grave' is measured by the penas cominadas: the smaller maximum, then the smaller minimum (F-g0-18's measure of the heavier).

citations.cite: CP art. 29, § 2º — "ser-lhe-á aplicada a pena deste"

readings.description: 'Menos grave' is judged on the crimes themselves (the interest injured, the manner), not only on their penalties.

taken.rationale: The paragraph's consequence is a penalty ('a pena deste'), so the comparison it presupposes is of penalties. The encoding measures as g0 did for the heaviest qualified form, and a crime of equal pena is not 'menos grave'.

witnesses: cp-g1a-concurso-testes.l4: `o comparsa que quis crime de igual pena` receives the pena of the crime committed
notes: The helper repeats F-g0-18's measure because g1a may not import g3's module; the conductor can merge them.

site.anchor: a circunstância se comunica aos demais concorrentes (art. 30)

source.quote: Art. 30 - Não se comunicam as circunstâncias e as condições de caráter pessoal, salvo quando elementares do crime.

readings.description: Art. 30 decides only whether the circumstance communicates; a participant who did not know of an elementary circumstance errs on an element of the tipo, and art. 20 excludes his dolo.
Art. 30 itself requires that the other participant knew of the elementary circumstance for it to communicate.

taken.rationale: Art. 30's words say nothing of knowledge; the Code already answers ignorance of an element in art. 20. Both readings give the same result for the participant.

site.anchor: crime cometido sem violência ou grave ameaça à pessoa (art. 16)

source.quote: Nos crimes cometidos sem violência ou grave ameaça à pessoa, reparado o dano ou restituída a coisa, até o recebimento da denúncia ou da queixa, por ato voluntário do agente, a pena será reduzida de um a dois terços. (Redação dada pela Lei nº 7.209, de 11.7.1984)

readings.description: The violence and grave threat that bar art. 16 are those used as the means of the conduct against a person; violence against a thing (a broken lock), a threat that is not grave, and an injury that results only from negligence do not bar it.

citations.cite: CP art. 16 — "cometidos sem violência ou grave ameaça à pessoa"

readings.description: Any violent result to a person, even a negligent one, bars art. 16.
readings.foreclosure: The text speaks of crimes 'cometidos sem violência', the manner of commission, not of their results. Whether the courts apply art. 16 to negligent crimes with a violent result was not searched.

taken.rationale: `crime cometido sem violência ou grave ameaça à pessoa (art. 16)` reads the shared `Fato`'s `meios empregados` for `violência à pessoa` and `grave ameaça`, and nothing else.

witnesses: cp-g1a-crime-testes.l4: `o furto com rompimento` and `a ameaça simples` admit the reduction; `o roubo com violência` and `o roubo com grave ameaça` do not

site.anchor: há situação de necessidade (art. 24)

source.quote: para salvar de perigo atual, que não provocou por sua vontade, nem podia de outro modo evitar, direito próprio ou alheio, cujo sacrifício, nas circunstâncias, não era razoável exigir-se. (Redação dada pela Lei nº 7.209, de 11.7.1984)

readings.description: Only a current danger opens estado de necessidade; the Code wrote 'atual ou iminente' in art. 25 and only 'atual' in art. 24.
An imminent danger is already a current one for art. 24's purpose, since waiting would defeat the rescue.

taken.rationale: The finding carries the Code's word 'atual'; whether an imminent danger is current is the fact-finder's to say. The contrast with art. 25 is recorded, not decided.

delegated_field: `Crime cometido no estrangeiro`'s `o agente é brasileiro`, in cp-g1a-aplicacao.l4

site.anchor: hipótese do art. 7º, II

source.quote: b) praticados por brasileiro; (Incluído pela Lei nº 7.209, de 1984)

readings.description: Brazilian nationality (the agent's under II, b; the victim's under § 3º) is taken at the time of the crime (art. 4º).
Nationality acquired or lost after the crime counts, as of the time of the prosecution.

taken.rationale: The fields' heralds are read at the time of the crime, the Code's time of the crime being art. 4º's; the fact-supplier certifies the nationality then.
